report:
Reviewed all five test entries and all local-symbol implementation associations. Requirements are: definition identity is determined by identity fields; independently changing CST, placement spans and derived signature/member/body facts does not alter it; unchanged sibling consumers can be reused; actual identity changes remain distinguishable.

Implementation inspection: LocalFnSym, LocalConstSym and LocalTypeAliasSym use name, scope and optional associated owner as untracked identity fields; CST and absolute span are tracked inputs. Struct, enum, trait and static symbols similarly separate name/scope from CST/span. Impl and macro invocation identity retain scope while CST/span are tracked. Use symbols retain scope while imports, attributes and span are tracked. Macro definitions retain name/scope while attributes, tokens and span are tracked. Module identity retains name, edition and parent; body source, attributes and span are tracked. Enum variants retain parent/name while individual copied CST, span and tuple shape are tracked, and tuple constructors identify the variant and name. Semantic signatures, items, fields and function bodies are separate symbol-keyed tracked functions rather than identity fields. Associated lowering selects owner/kind/name/occurrence keys and constructs functions/types/constants with that owner; moving an unrelated sibling does not change the selected key. Added essential local_identity associations for the other kind declarations and associated-item key producer so these files participate in subsequent freshness checks. Captured parser and test infrastructure show source edits update the same input/database, constructors receive separate identity and detail fields, ObservedSymbol interns the actual symbol, and the query log records WillExecute events.

Test inspection: detail_edits_preserve_local_symbol_query_keys has twelve cases, covering function body, struct/enum field types, trait member signature, impl member body, alias target, const/static initializer, module attributes, use import, macro definition tokens and invocation arguments. It asserts represented non-error items, empty warm query logs, and no identity observer execution after each detail edit. enum_detail_edits_preserve_variant_query_keys changes a tuple variant field type and checks no variant/constructor identity observer execution. The associated-item matrix covers functions, types and constants in traits and impls under both insertion and reordering, asserts the owner, and checks observer reuse in both edit directions; it therefore exercises placement changes and unchanged sibling identities. New local_function_identity_changes_are_distinguishable proves a name change executes the identity observer again (with an explicit cold-observer control and new-name assertion), and same-name functions in distinct scopes compare unequal while their names compare equal. These checks would detect detail fields accidentally joining identity or name/scope distinctions disappearing.

The explicit TODO symbols_local_identity remains justified and deferred: the exhaustive per-kind sibling insertion/reordering and signature/member/body consumer-reuse matrix is not present. Its prerequisite is extending the existing edit fixtures with consumers of each independently tracked semantic fact and execution assertions for unchanged siblings. Current ordinary tests establish the represented detail and associated movement cases, not exhaustive reuse of every semantic operation for every kind. No N/A or implementation TODO entry exists; this report does not promote the TODO placeholder into behavioral evidence.

Executed cargo fmt, cargo build (success), cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib local_function_identity_changes_are_distinguishable (1 passed), and cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib preserve (10 passed, including all three existing ordinary tests). An initial compilation of the new test found ambiguous into() inference; it was corrected with explicit Symbol::from and the successful command rerun before this fresh review. This was a test compilation issue, not a reproduced semantic defect. No production behavior changed. Central delegated post-codegen and Sage sanity reviews remain the coordinator's integration responsibility.
